title: Quantitative methods for finance: calculus, matrices and optimization
audience: a college student in a finance, accounting or business degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Use derivatives and integrals for marginal analysis and continuous compounding, series for annuities, matrices and vectors for portfolios and systems of equations, and unconstrained and constrained optimization with Lagrange multipliers.

weeks.4: Integrals and present value of continuous flows
weeks.8: Systems of equations and matrix inverses

blocks.deliverable: Find marginal cost and revenue for three firms.
Derive the present value of an annuity from a series.
Week 7 midterm; solve a pricing system with matrices.
Find the minimum-variance weights for two assets.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Optimization project: for a set of three to five assets with given expected returns and covariances, derive and compute the minimum-variance portfolio and one target-return portfolio, verify the answer numerically in Python, and explain each step of the mathematics.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.

files.L04.txt: Integrals and present value of continuous flows
files.L08.txt: Systems of equations and matrix inverses
